label: <DEL> step in long sequences whose first token is a digit 0-2 or z/h/j/n/m
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (97% of activation mass, 96% of active steps). It is active at only 12% of delimiter steps. Two things set the rate there: sequence length (rate and mass rise steeply with L; L=8-9 carry 85% of mass, L<=5 is almost silent) and the first original token, which is what gets output at the delimiter. Rates are highest when that token is digit 0, 1 or 2, then z, h, j, n, m, and fall off gradually for the other letters, so the dependence is graded rather than a clean set. Sequences with more digits are somewhat more likely to fire. The top activations are all L=8-9 sequences that start with a digit. A small leftover (about 3% of mass) appears on the last one or two original-phase tokens of length-9 sequences, just before <DEL>. Never active in the copy phase or early in the original phase. Restricting to delimiter and L>=7 gives recall 0.91 but precision 0.23. Adding the first-token set trades recall for precision (dev F1 0.57, mass recall 0.69).
